failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: After hop 1 query 'Leafcutter John Polar Bear electronics Same as You album British experimental jazz', the coordinator generated query for hop 2 'Leafcutter John Polar Bear electronics Same as You album British experimental jazz' (identical wording), and for hop 3 generated 'No query needed - claim fully verified by both summaries.' Despite both summaries stating full verification after hop 1, the system continued executing retrievals that fetched redundant documents (hop 2 returned the same Polar Bear passages plus other Polar Bear albums; hop 3 returned unrelated documents about longevity claims and database query languages).

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1 solver reasoning, the solver explicitly states 'Passages [3], [4], [5], [6], and [7] are not relevant to this claim as they discuss different artists and songs' yet the passages were provided and required the solver to scan and dismiss them (Device album, One Direction song, Portugal. The Man, Louis Tomlinson song, Jessie J song). Similarly in hop 3, the system retrieved 10 documents entirely unrelated to the claim (longevity claims, database management systems, query languages) that would require processing to determine irrelevance.

failure_modes.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
failure_modes.evidence: The solver produced nearly identical summaries across hops: Summary 1 states 'The claim is fully verified by the provided passages. Leafcutter John is confirmed to be a member of Polar Bear...All elements of the claim are directly supported by passages [1] and [2].' Summary 2 states 'The claim can be fully verified with the provided passages. Passage [1] explicitly identifies Leafcutter John as the electronics player in Polar Bear...All key entities mentioned in the claim...are directly addressed in the passages.' Both summaries reach identical conclusions with only minor rephrasing, showing circular restatement without progression.
